walkthroughs.body_html:
Transverse waves: vibration is at right angles to wave direction. Examples: water ripples, light, all EM waves.

Longitudinal waves: vibration is along the wave direction. Example: sound.

Longitudinal waves have compressions (squashed bits) and rarefactions (stretched bits).

Wave speed = frequency x wavelength.

Sound in air ≈ 340 m/s.
Sound in water ≈ 1500 m/s.
Light in air ≈ 300,000,000 m/s.

Light is so fast we see lightning before we hear thunder!

Waves are everywhere:

Ultrasound - baby scans, cleaning jewellery, sonar.
Radio waves - phones, TV, Wi-Fi.
Microwaves - cooking, satellites.
Infrared - remote controls, heat cameras.

Each type carries energy from one place to another.

mcqs.q: Why is the electric field between parallel charged plates considered uniform?
options: The field still decreases with the inverse square of distance — uniform just means it's smooth.
Because the plates are uniform in shape.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
Field strength is constant in magnitude and direction throughout the region (away from edges), unlike the inverse-square field of a point charge.
